headline: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund
body: **Anthropic** says it will commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, a wholly-owned entity within the company. It has the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in its value. The company says it will share more on structure and governance in the coming months.
note: The fund is still mostly a shape without rules: the uses are broad, and who decides which projects get money is not yet public. Anthropic's CEO has described the industry's public sentiment as a crisis of trust, and this is one of the company's answers.

figure.label: share of Anthropic's shares committed to the fund

evidence.text: Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value.
Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.
And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
The AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”
If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.
